newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Russia '96 sunseed output seen 3.5 mln T.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Russia '96 sunseed output seen 3.5 mln T.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
SOVECON ESTIMATES RUSSIAN 1996 SUNFLOWER SEED OUTPUT AT ABOUT 3.5 MILLION TONNES AFTER 4.2 MILLION IN 1995

MOSCOW, Sept 26 - Despite some decline in domestic prices, sunflower seed remains one of Russia's most profitable crops, and sunflower seed exports are a major source of hard currency earnings for Russian farmers.
In 1996, a delayed spring followed by very hot weather seriously affected sunflower seed sowing in the North Caucasus, particularly in Rostov oblast.
As a result, Russia's 1996 total area sown to sunflowers declined to 3.9 million hectares, after 4.1 million in 1995, due mainly to a decline in plantings in the North Caucasus.
Plantings increased in other sunflower-producing areas, except West Siberia (Table 1).
In 1996, the sunflower seed harvest started later than last year.
By September 18, about four percent of planted area had been harvested, 146,300 ha. At the same time last year 438,500 ha had been harvested.

Forecasts at this stage are quite tentative, but lower sunflower seed yields at the beginning of the harvest in the North Caucasus (Table 2) indicate a very likely decline in yields in this region against year-ago levels.
As a result, SovEcon forecasts sunflower seed output in the region at 1.7-1.8 million tonnes, versus 2.4 million tonnes in 1995.
In Povolzhsk, sunflower seed yields are expected to be close to last year's level. Output is forecast at 0.75-0.8 million tonnes, versus 0.8 million tonnes in 1995.
Assuming normal harvest progress, Central-Chernozem sunflower seed production is anticipated to be about 0.65-0.7 million tonnes, versus 0.73 million tonnes in 1995.
As a result, SovEcon provisionally forecasts 1996 sunflower seed output in Russia at about 3.5-3.6 million tonnes, after 4.2 million in 1995, or some 15 percent lower.
However, 1996 output will be the second largest in the 1990s, and Russia is likely to continue its sunflower seed exports in 1996-1997, especially in light of sunflower seed crop failure in Ukraine.
